correctness.rationale: For dimension at least three, Sarkar's contraction argument shows that an automorphism of the point blow-up descends after contracting all \((-1)\)-hypersurfaces. An abelian variety has no rational curves and therefore no \((-1)\)-hypersurfaces, so the contraction is the original blow-down. Every automorphism of the abelian variety is translation followed by a group automorphism; the group-automorphism part is countable because \(\operatorname{End}(A)\) is a finite-rank free abelian group. For each group automorphism and each permutation of a triple, the stabilizer condition is a closed kernel in \(A^3\) and is proper unless both are identities. A very general triple avoids the countable union. The lower bound is given by the explicit involutions \(x\mapsto 2p-x\) and \(x\mapsto p+q-x\).
risks: The proof is scoped to complex abelian varieties of dimension at least three; no positive-characteristic claim is made.

value.rationale: The source's central problem is to determine how many very general point blow-ups are needed to kill automorphisms. On abelian varieties of dimension at least three, the finding replaces the source's dimension-dependent sufficient bound \(d+1\) by the exact constant three and proves sharpness with explicit one- and two-point involutions. The cutoff is intrinsic to the geometry of the automorphism group and is not an arbitrary parameter slice.
risks: The theorem does not classify special triples or extend to positive characteristic.
